terms.gloss: to be the object of (a verb), literally to be joined to it
terms.grammar: passive of adjungō, with the dative of the verb
terms.comment: Traupman notes that the Roman grammarians never used objectum of the object of a verb or preposition (247). Where we say that a word is the object of the verb, he says it is joined to it: hic homō verbō adjungitur (247), and Cui nōminī adjungitur? for a preposition, what noun is its object? (243). We have not found the construction in Lewis & Short.

phrases.english: What noun is its object? — The noun “ōrīs”.
“The man” is the object of the verb.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 239, 243, 247, 352.
